newsitem.title: CANADA: U.S. strike unlikely to affect Canada, UPS says.
newsitem.headline: U.S. strike unlikely to affect Canada, UPS says.

text.p: A nationwide strike by U.S. employees at United Parcel Service of America Inc will have no significant effect on Canadian customers, an official with the company's Canadian unit said on Tuesday.

"All services within Canada in terms of pickup and delivery are normal and we are expecting little impact on packages going to the U.S. and international destinations," said United Parcel Service Canada Ltd spokeswoman Susan Bortot.
However, she conceded that the company could not guarantee the time of delivery, which it usually does, on Canadian packages destined for the United States.

About 190,000 UPS America drivers, loaders and sorters belonging to the International Brotherhood of Teamsters walked off the job early Monday morning after talks between the union and the company collapsed.
UPS handles more than 60 percent of all U.S. parcel deliveries and about 80 percent of all small shipments
The company's 5,900 employees in Canada have stayed on the job because of an existing contract between the Teamsters and UPS Canada.
"We have a completely separate agreement ratified in April that takes us into the next century," Bortot said.

Industry analysts observed that a protracted U.S. strike could allow competitors, such as Federal Express Canada Ltd and Purolator Courier Ltd, a division of Canada Post Corp, to muscle in on UPS' market share in Canada.

Federal Express Canada reported a higher number of inquiries and new customer calls since the beginning of the strike, but said it would not reduce the quality of its services to take on new customers.

"The existing customers have to be protected, and we will do what we can in terms of staffing up and increasing hours, making more drop-off spots available," said Lisa Elliott, manager of corporate communications with Federal Express Canada in Mississauga, Ontario.
"In the event of a long, drawn-out strike, we will also consider airlifts," Elliott said.
